janson-problem-20-3-conditioned-box-coun.why: Matches parts (a) and (b) of the record: a fixed tilt with tau < rho, or tau = rho with finite variance, conditioning at m_n - n mu = O(1) (the hypothesis the record's own proof uses), and the same diagonal and off-diagonal covariances jointly over a finite D. Excluding lambda = 0 and requiring sigma^2 > 0 only drops the degenerate point where the formula divides by zero, and Janson's own problem says 0 < lambda < nu. The identifications Psi(t) = t Phi'(t)/Phi(t), lambda = mu and nu = lim Psi are correct. The proof text is the record's (a) and (b) verbatim, with no invented steps.

janson-problem-20-3-irregular-tail-nonno.why: The draft states the record's conclusion more weakly than the record does. (1) The record says the formula 'fails in general' in regimes (c) and (d) and calls 20.3 answered 'no' there. The draft downgrades this to 'a proposed obstruction' and says 'no explicit counterexample construction is certified', which misstates the record's claim instead of recording its dependency. The honest form keeps the record's strength and makes the reliance on the companion memo explicit as a hypothesis. (2) The record says the limits converge ('converges to', 'asymptotically'); the draft weakens this to a 'subsequential limit'. (3) The draft drops the record's positive half: in regimes (c) and (d) the would-be formula is sigma_d^2 = pi_d(1-pi_d), and it holds under regular variation, via Thevenin's Theorem 6.7 for (d). (4) The draft takes 'pi with mean nu' as a generic law, but in the record pi is the tilted law at tau = rho and nu = lim Psi. The draft also omits the record's framing that the dividing line between the regimes is local flatness of the tail.
janson-problem-20-3-irregular-tail-nonno.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; depends on the companion memo on Problem 20.2] This is the boundary and condensation part of the answer recorded for Svante Janson's Problem 20.3 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510. Use Janson's balls-in-boxes setting with weights w_j, generating function Phi, radius rho, Psi(t) = t Phi'(t)/Phi(t), nu = lim_{t up to rho} Psi(t), m/n -> lambda, pi the tilted law at tau = rho when lambda >= nu, and N_d the number of boxes with d balls. In the two regimes not covered by the finite-variance mean-conditioning theorem, (c) lambda = nu with sigma^2 = infinity and (d) lambda > nu, the natural analogue of the Gaussian limit has variance sigma_d^2 = pi_d(1-pi_d). In (d) the constraint is absorbed by the condensate rather than by the bulk. The record asserts that this analogue holds under regular variation of the tail, by the argument of Thevenin's Theorem 6.7 in case (d), and fails in general. The failure rests on two constructions, Theorems A and B of the companion memo on Problem 20.2. Theorem A is a subcritical law conditioned at lambda = 1 > nu, that is, sum of the xi_i equal to n-1, for which (N_1 - n pi_1)/sqrt(n) converges to a non-degenerate two-point law. Theorem B is a law with nu = 1 and sigma^2 = infinity, conditioned at lambda = 1, for which (N_1 - n pi_1)/sqrt(n) converges to a mixture of two Gaussians. Assuming those two theorems, a Gaussian limit for the box counts in regimes (c) and (d) does not hold without a further regularity condition on the tail. The record identifies local flatness of the tail at the scale the conditioning must supply as the dividing line. This is an unrefereed campaign result, and the counterexamples are proved in the companion memo, not in this record.

janson-problem-20-4-single-vertex-fringe.why: The draft leaves out the record's actual reduction step and conclusion, and it never sets up the random model. The record argues as follows: N_bullet = N_0. In both Problem 20.2 constructions the bulk is carried by degrees 0 and 1, so N_0 = n - N_1 + O(1). The leaf count therefore inherits the non-Gaussian behaviour of N_1. Hence, for nu < 1 and for nu = 1 with sigma^2 = infinity, fringe-subtree counts are not asymptotically normal in general. The draft keeps only a hypothetical ('a proved failure ... would') and says the record 'supplies no ... proof of the needed leaf-count limit', which misreports what the record gives. The draft should instead state the record's argument, conditional on the memo's constructions. Also, T_n should be the size-conditioned Galton-Watson (simply generated) tree, not just any ordered tree. Leaving the Janson 2016 finite-variance answer out as literature is fine.
janson-problem-20-4-single-vertex-fringe.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; depends on the companion memo on Problem 20.2] This is the negative part of the answer recorded for Svante Janson's Problem 20.4 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510. Problem 20.4 asks for a Gaussian extension of Theorem 7.12, the law of large numbers for fringe-subtree counts. Let T_n be the simply generated tree, equivalently the conditioned Galton-Watson tree, with n vertices. Let N_T be the number of vertices whose fringe subtree equals a fixed finite ordered rooted tree T, and let N_d be the number of vertices with d children. For the one-vertex tree bullet, N_bullet = N_0 exactly, since its occurrences are precisely the leaves. In both constructions of the companion memo on Problem 20.2, the subcritical law of its Theorem A (nu < 1) and the critical infinite-variance law of its Theorem B (nu = 1, sigma^2 = infinity), the bulk of the vertices has degree 0 or 1. Hence N_0 = n - N_1 + O(1), and N_bullet inherits the non-Gaussian limit of (N_1 - n pi_1)/sqrt(n): a two-point law in the first construction and a mixture of two Gaussians in the second. Assuming those two theorems, fringe-subtree counts are not asymptotically normal in general when nu < 1, nor when nu = 1 with sigma^2 = infinity. The finite-variance critical case is resolved in the literature by Janson (Random Structures Algorithms 48, 2016, Theorem 1.5) and is not included here as own work. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
